items.title: Once a conversation passes 12 turns, every chat turn writes its whole history to the prompt cache again
items.what_the_person_sees: Nothing on screen; each quick turn pays the cache-write price on about 1,900-2,000 history tokens (about 40% of a quick Haiku turn's bill), more on Sonnet thorough passes.
items.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/c15.json (k2 read 16,128 wrote 1,915; k4 read 16,128 wrote 2,028; 25 messages each, 0 identical leading messages between k1 and k2); /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/steps/LC-C15.json; repro /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-chat-16/repro.mts (PromptCacheSim: 4->5 turns read 2,720/write 59; 13->14 read 2,462/write 741).
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:379 const recent = turns.slice(-HISTORY_TURNS) (HISTORY_TURNS 12, :267) and the token-cap loop dropping the oldest turn one at a time, so the first message changes on every turn and the prefix cache matches only tools and system; called from agent.ts:1605-1607 (quick) and :1630 (thorough, THOROUGH_HISTORY_TOKENS 8,000).
items.fix_sketch: A stepped window, a pure function of the stored rows: start = max(0, floor((n - HISTORY_TURNS) / K) * K) with K = 6 by the turn's index from the conversation's start (seq, not the position in the 100-turn read), so the window holds 12 to 17 turns and moves every 6 turns; the token cap drops turns in blocks anchored to the same start (or keeps the start until the budget plus a margin is passed), never one per call; the same for the thorough pass; the same after a restart. Update runtime.md ('History').
items.test_boundary: Composed (packages/runtime/test/chat-depth.test.ts 'caching' or beside conversation.test.ts's history-cache case) with FakeProvider({promptCache: {minTokens: 1}}): 13 seeded turns, two quick lines within 5 simulated minutes: the second request's messages[0] equals the first's and its cache_read_input_tokens covers the first request's history; a second case under 12 turns whose long replies trip the token cap; a restart case (compose twice) gives the same window.
items.notes: Money (small, every turn). LC-C15's step key is here; its thorough part passed; its retraction of true statements is L4-chat-106. A breakpoint before the newest turns would not help (the change is at message 0).

items.title: After the person presses Answer now, the answer offers 'This needs a stronger model ... Go ahead?'
items.what_the_person_sees: '... which conflicts with these records.' then 'This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.04 (at most CHF 0.17) and 10 seconds. Go ahead?' with Go ahead, under 'Thought it through more carefully · 5 s · under CHF 0.01', although they chose to have it answer now (and that Go ahead loops, L4-chat-201).
items.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/c16b.json (POST /chat/turns/.../answer-now at 08:52:46.445; first call USD 0.001046 of a USD 0.125 budget), 76-c16c-after-restart.png; probe /tmp/frbench/l4c18/pkg/test/l4c18.test.ts (fails at 4cf11fd with the offer).
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1776 entry.answerNow = () => budget.wrapUpNow(o.runId); packages/runtime/src/enforcement/budget.ts:266-270 merges a wrap-up by spend and by wrapUpNow (:283) into one decision; the loop sets wrapUpSent either way; agent.ts:2253 adds the next rung's offer on deep && !stopped && result?.wrapUpSent && !offer.
items.fix_sketch: Record why the wrap-up came: SessionBudget.precheck stores line.wrappedBy = spend over the line ? 'line' : 'now' and exposes wrapReasonOf(runId) (append-only); agent.ts:2253 also requires wrapReasonOf(runId) === 'line'. (Smaller alternative: answerNow sets a flag when wrapUpNow returns true; a press after the budget already wrapped returns false and keeps the offer.) The Answer-now reply carries and stores no offer. Update runtime.md's rung paragraph and ADR 0114's amendment ('reached its wrap-up' means its budget line, never Answer now).
items.test_boundary: Composed chat-depth.test.ts, the existing 'Answer now during a longer pass' case gains expect(r.offer).toBeNull() and the row's offer null; control: a longer pass whose second call crosses its budget line (no press) still gets the stronger ask line; real-daemon: client.answerNow(turnId) during 'think it through' leaves no offer and no Go ahead in the conversation view.

A joined project (archived with joined_into) still counts through its keeper. The "removed" verdict (the marker names the person's own removed project; run C session lead decision 14, took_over with removed true) is unchanged: verdictOf finds it through index.row before knows is asked. project.ts's Undo is not changed: the index fix also covers rows stored this way already. items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:875 scaffoldInCopy calls this.checkout(project, target, "fr/docs-scaffold", { ours }) with no `fresh`, so checkout (:1249-1254) starts the copy from origin/fr/docs-scaffold whenever that ref exists, here a closed pull request's branch carrying a third project's marker. mark() (:1427-1440) keeps that marker (status other_project, only a WARN log), scaffoldDocs finds every doc present, so nothing is written: no commit, no push (:921, never forced), no pull request. The outcome (prUrl null, marker other_project) is only recorded: create-project.ts:192 -> scaffoldProjectDocs (:204-216) ignores it; compose.ts:4916-4924 repositoryTakeOver.writeMarker sets failed only when the scaffold throws; no screen reads marker.status. writeSessionStatus already passes `fresh: async (open) => !open` (:983) and pushes with `force: !existingPr` (:998). C4L-2: with this project's own scaffold pull request open, the run comments only the missing docs (:922-928) and commits the replaced marker on top of the old branch instead of rebuilding it on the default branch.
items.fix_sketch: 1) scaffoldInCopy passes `fresh: async (open) => !open`, as writeSessionStatus: with no open scaffold pull request of this project the branch starts from origin/<default branch>. Branch rule (D-L4-24, the plan check): Forerunner never force-pushes over a branch it did not write for this project. When origin/fr/docs-scaffold exists and is not this project's own (its marker names another project, or it has none), the scaffold opens its own branch fr/docs-scaffold-<project slug> from origin/<default branch> and pushes it without force; the old branch and its closed pull request stay as they are. A force-push (with a lease on the head just read, never the default branch) replaces only this project's own scaffold branch, as writeSessionStatus does for fr/status (:983, :998); Docs and the take-over find the scaffold pull request on either name; when no pull request could open, the outcome says why. Another project's open pull request stays `foreign` (W15-01: never written to or commented on). 2) C4L-2: a take-over while this project's own scaffold pull request is open rebuilds that branch on the default branch under the copy's lock, writes the replaced marker, force-pushes this project's own branch and comments tookOverLine on the pull request (ADR 0117's amendment). 3) Said where the person reads the take-over: compose.ts writeMarker returns failed (or a new notOpened) when prUrl is null and nothing was written, so repo.take_over answers tookOverNoPullRequestSentence; POST /projects with takeOver records the same on the row and the Overview's take-over line reads that GitHub still names "Kite club" because the docs pull request could not be opened; Docs does not read "8 of 8 present" as if the take-over had landed. 4) Sibling (validation rule 8): packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts:2521-2533 writeDocsToRepository starts fr/intake-<id>-docs from the default branch when no pull request is open but pushes without force (`force: !!existingPr`), so an old branch of the same name refuses the push: the same branch rule (fr/intake-<id>-docs carries the intake's own id, so an old branch of that name is this project's own and is replaced with a lease). 5) docs/maintainers/runtime.md (the scaffold branch's start rule), ADR 0117 dated amendment.
items.test_boundary: Composed daemon test in packages/runtime/test/docs-scaffold.test.ts (MemoryGitHost and a bare repository, app.request), in the OR-06/OR-15 describe: o/kite's main has the doc set and Kite club's marker, and an fr/docs-scaffold branch not in main carries a third project's marker with its pull request closed. POST /projects without takeOver answers 409; with takeOver {projects:[KITE]} 201. Expect exactly one open pull request, on fr/docs-scaffold-<slug> (the old fr/docs-scaffold's head unchanged), whose body has the take-over line, its marker names the new project, main is an ancestor of the branch and the diff to main is only .forerunner/project.json (today: no pull request). Second case (C4L-2): this project's own scaffold pull request open, then repo.take_over through POST /commands: the branch is rebuilt on main with the replaced marker and the pull request gets the take-over line. Third: a host refusal at the push: repo.take_over's sentence reads 'Took over o/kite from "Kite club" here, but the docs pull request that names this project could not be opened, so GitHub still names "Kite club".' and the Overview line says so (real-daemon case through client.project, describe "l4-github-link, run L4"). A fr/docs-scaffold that is not this project's own (a closed pull request's branch with another project's marker, or one with no marker) is never force-pushed; this project's own scaffold branch is replaced with a lease.
items.notes: Same root cause from two sources: the scaffold branch is not started from the default branch (L4-github-1 with no open pull request; C4L-2 with this project's own open one), so they are one item. Severity major, not blocker: the project works in the app, but the take-over's promise silently does not happen on GitHub, and an old head branch of a closed pull request is GitHub's default. Wider effect (reasoned from the code, not run): any new project on a repository with an old fr/docs-scaffold branch that lacks some docs would add them on top of the old commit and open a pull request carrying another project's marker. The brief path (PR #50) was not affected: the intake writes its own fr/intake-<id>-docs branch. Plan check (D-L4-24): the earlier rule allowed a force-push over any closed or merged pull request's branch, which can be another project's or another person's; no decision recorded that, so the scaffold now takes its own branch name instead and force-pushes only its own branch.

items.evidence: live4:L4-l3-10 (l3 journey screenshots 08-kt-new-offer, 11-kt-statuspr-after; l3a home app-status/docs/status.md; the sandbox had no open pull request after the session); live4-step:l3:LC-L3.L3-github-6 (observed: the status words are right, no status pull request because the project is shared, although Settings said it would go to GitHub).
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/daemon/settings-view.ts:315-325 shows the "Status pull request" row with Change whenever onHostRepository(p), never asking isTogether; packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:403-418 status_pull_request's effect ignores the project and settings.set has no together refusal, so Settings, chat and voice get the same false read-back. items.fix_sketch: (a) At the command, so chat and voice get it too: settings.set status_pull_request=true on a together project (isTogether from @forerunner/runtime/sources/repository-words) is refused in one sentence with nothing written: 'You work on "Kite flyers" together with another Forerunner, so its status stays in the app (Docs, Status); no status pull request is opened.' (details {key, cause: "together"}); turning it off still acts. (b) settings-view.ts shows the row only when onHostRepository(p) && !isTogether(p), as C-57 hides it for a linked folder. (c) apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts mirrors both. (d) The user guide's "Working with someone on one repository" section and docs/maintainers (settings, docs).
items.test_boundary: Real-daemon case (describe "l4-github-link, run L4", or extend packages/runtime/test/onerepo-together.test.ts's two-home case): after Work together on o/kite, GET /settings has no project.status_pull_request row for the project; POST /commands settings.set {key:"status_pull_request", value:true, project} answers refused with the exact sentence, the change log gains no row and the setting is unchanged; the same through chat's settings_set tool (commands unit with the executor). items.title: A first plan whose reply leaves out the docs is taken without asking again, so the plan card has no decision line
items.what_the_person_sees: A new project's plan card normally shows "Decision: ..." (the drafted docs/decisions/0001) before Approve and start. If the model's first-plan reply leaves out "docs" entirely, the card shows no decision, the project gets only template docs and no decision record, and nothing asks the model again.
items.evidence: C2:CL-6 (leftovers-C2.json, d1109-onerepo-link's review). Code at 4cf11fd only.
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts:237-242 IntakeProposalBody has `docs: IntakeDocs.default({})` for both forms (OR-08 made it optional for the plan-only form); parse at :821 then accepts a first-plan reply without docs, although the first-plan rules (:1996-2013) ask for docs/decisions/0001-<slug>.md whose "Decision:" line the card shows. The cut-off retry advice (:811) tells the model to "leave docs out".
items.fix_sketch: The parse knows the form: in the first-plan form a reply without docs/decisions/0001-<slug>.md is refused with one problem line for the one retry, e.g. 'docs: the decision record is missing: write docs/decisions/0001-<slug>.md with the choice the brief points to; any standard doc you leave out is written from the template.'; the plan-only form keeps the default {}. The cut-off advice keeps the record and drops the rest: 'Write each doc in a few lines, or leave out the standard docs (Forerunner writes them from its templates), but keep docs/decisions/0001 short.' Both are model-facing text: assert them exactly. If the retry also lacks it, the card is filed without a decision line as today (no third call).
items.test_boundary: packages/runtime/test/intake.test.ts through the intake route with the stand-in model: a first-plan reply without docs makes the one retry, whose request carries the exact problem line; the second reply with the record lands a card whose decision line the Inbox shows (real-daemon client.inbox, describe "l4-github-link, run L4"); a plan-only (Add to) reply without docs is still taken at once; the cut-off advice's exact text.
items.notes: A prompt the app sends (the cut-off advice "leave docs out") makes the missing record likely, so this is a fix in the app, not model-only. intake.ts is shared: this area owns IntakeProposalBody, the parse and the retry/cut-off problem lines only.

items.title: Work together's "since" time is read from the computer's clock directly, and the folder scan reads a marker outside its injected file access

items.title: The other-host refusal always names github.com, and the line under Take it over can pass 100 characters
items.what_the_person_sees: On an install set up for a GitHub Enterprise host, linking a repository elsewhere answers "Forerunner works with repositories on github.com, not <host>.", which is untrue there. With a 60-character project name in the marker, the line under Take it over ("The repository then names this project: choose it only if no Forerunner uses "<name>" now.") runs to about 125 characters (design section 5 rule 1: a consequence line is at most 100).
items.evidence: C2:CL-8 (leftovers-C2.json). AGENTS.md: nothing hardcoded to one host.
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/sources/repository-words.ts:190-192 otherHostSentence hardcodes "github.com"; :180-182 takeOverLine quotes the marker's whole name.
items.fix_sketch: otherHostSentence takes the configured web host (from config.githubApiBase, "github.com" by default) from its callers. takeOverLine cuts the quoted name at a word (balancedCut with cutWords, about 30 characters) so the line stays at most 100 characters, or reads 'The repository then names this project. Choose it only if nobody uses "<name>" now.'.

items.title: The plan's docs pull request branch carries the project's full id (fr/intake-<uuid>-docs)

items.title: A pull request merged on GitHub that still held a closed task's work: that task still reads "closed without merging", and nothing offers to take its change out of main
items.what_the_person_sees: Task B builds on task A. A's pull request is closed on GitHub, then B's is merged on GitHub's website before Forerunner looks. A's change is now on main through B, but A's Tasks row and record say "#A was closed without merging.", no card says its change reached main, and the only way out is Take this work out on B, which removes both.
items.evidence: L3:LL-4 (leftovers-L3.json); /tmp/frbench/runL3-l3-merge-fix.json not_done[0] (L3-github-1 part 3, with the fixer's fix idea); ADR 0111 amendment of 2026-11-15 point 4 ("left for later").
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/dependent-branches.ts:208-232 mergedOnHost moves only the merged task's record and rebuilds what built on it; :234-243 closedOnHost moves A's record to left_to_you/"closed" without asking whether A's reviewed change reached the default branch through a merged dependent.
items.fix_sketch: When the watcher sees a pull request merged on GitHub (mergedOnHost) or a dependency closed (closedOnHost), each dependency of the merged one whose record is not merged is checked: if its reviewed head is an ancestor of the merge commit (git merge-base --is-ancestor in the copy under the copy's lock, or GitHub's compare), its record moves to merged with last_outcome "merged_through" and method null, sentence '#46 was closed, but its change reached main through #48.' (no migration: last_outcome is free text). Its row reads "Accepted · merged through #48"; one card says it with Take this work out (merged-actions' take-out of A's commits) and Keep it. Order-independent (whichever event the watcher reads first), idempotent across a restart; nothing is written to GitHub before the person presses. ADR 0111 point 4 replaced by a dated amendment; runtime.md.
items.test_boundary: Composed test in packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts (chainWorld): A, then B depending on A; close A on the fake host, merge B on the host, one poll; the reverse order; and a restart between. A's record reads merged/merged_through, its Tasks row (GET /projects/:id/tasks) reads "merged through #2", one card whose requestView(row).options are the two buttons; answering Take this work out (with the option string) opens one take-out pull request that removes A's change and keeps B's. Real-daemon case for the card through client.inbox (describe "l4-github-merge, run L4").
items.notes: Major from its leftover (a wrong state the app states as fact). Rare (the person merges B on GitHub's website before a poll) but run L3's own amendment names it as what remains. Cut line inside the item: the Take this work out for A alone may end not_done if the take-out cannot revert a commit range (the card then offers Take this work out on #48 and says it removes both); the record's and the row's true words never.

(:762-770); the merge step finds out afterwards.

merged_from.title: Merge pressed just after a push answers 'Merging #62.', then refuses: the press checks the pull request's head, which GitHub updates late, not the branch
merged_from.what_the_person_sees: The answer is 'Merging #62.', and about 1.5 s later the row reads '#62 changed after the review ...'. Nothing is merged.
merged_from.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts:751-760: the head check reads the listing's head.sha (:756) and skips when it equals reviewed_head_sha (:757). packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:2094-2100: headMovedNow reads getPullRequest again, which lags the same way. Nothing reads the branch ref (host.getBranchHead).
merged_from.fix_sketch:
1. For each chain task with a reviewed_head_sha, read host.getBranchHead(ref, listedPr.head.ref). Call headMovedNow whenever either head differs from the reviewed commit.
2. In headMovedNow, a getPullRequest head equal to the reviewed commit never overrides a newer branch head that was passed in. keepsOwnChange and the rebuilt-by-Forerunner case still decide as they do today.
3. One more GET per chain task per press. The merge step's PUT, pinned to the sha, stays.
merged_from.test_boundary: packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts plus a real-daemon case. Give the fake git host a 'pull head lag' option (testenv/src/githost/ops.ts:296: the push moves refs at once, and the pull request's head.sha follows on a later read). Push to an accepted task's branch with the lag on, then press Merge at once through POST /projects/:id/pull-requests/:n/merge, as the Overview sends it. Expect {state:'refused', sentence:'#N changed after the review: ...'}, nothing merged, and one card.
merged_from.merge_reason: Same block: the press answers 'Merging #N.' before it reads the pull request's current state (pull-requests.ts:711-770); one read covers checks, mergeable state and the branch head.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts:76-83: NOTHING accepts a 'nothing' followed only by left/required words, by an ABOUT clause that must start with a preposition (for, in, by, under, within, to meet ...; :76) or by punctuation and a reason (:78); 'nothing [that] the criteria require' has neither, so isNothing (:92) is false and parseHandoff keeps it as an item (:176-207). packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1725-1732 then pauses (wrap-up sent and leftToDo not empty). The words the model hears invite the qualifier: WRAP_UP_BRIEF_LINE (budget-pause.ts:52-53: "'Left to do:' (only what the task's criteria still need ..., or 'nothing'; ...)") and wrapUpText (packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:106-110: 'Left to do: (only what the task's criteria still need, as a list with the next step first, or nothing; ...)').
items.fix_sketch: (1) budget-pause.ts: a relative-clause form after the left/required group, (?:\s+(?:that|which))?\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:task'?s\s+)?(?:(?:acceptance|two|three|\d+)\s+)?(?:criteri(?:a|on)|brief|task|scope|requirements?|deliverables?)(?:\s+(?:still|yet))?\s+(?:requires?|needs?|asks?\s+for|calls?\s+for|demands?), with ABOUT's reason tail; and the general rule that ends the one-phrasing-at-a-time patching (this is the third live phrasing after W15-14 and L3-research-1): a Left-to-do line that starts with nothing/none, names the whole set (WHOLE_SET) and has no NOT_NOTHING word is nothing. ONE_CRITERION and NOT_NOTHING stay ('nothing the criteria require yet: the tests fail' stays an item; 'nothing criterion 2 needs' says nothing of the rest). (2) Model-facing words, exact text on both drivers: WRAP_UP_BRIEF_LINE and wrapUpText ask for the single word 'nothing' as the whole list when the criteria are met; WRAP_UP_MARK, the trigger, the line, the reserve and the save-only rule unchanged. (3) ADR 0112's parse paragraph (dated amendment) and docs/maintainers/runtime.md's budget-pause section.
items.test_boundary: Composed runtime (packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts, beside the case 'a run that hears the wrap-up and lists only Nothing for the acceptance criteria ... is reviewed and done'): the stand-in researcher's post-wrap-up reply is LC-C7's seq 8 report word for word; expect the task reviewed and done in the same session, run outcomes ['completed'], no 'paused before' or 'listed one thing left to do' line in GET /sessions/:id/events, and no card for it in GET /inbox (today: the Continue card). parseHandoff unit cases for the live line and its siblings. Exact-text assertions of the brief line in the composed model-call log, of the wrap-up block at the request the fake provider receives (wrap-up.test.ts) and at PostToolUse's additionalContext (sdk-driver.test.ts).
items.notes: Not model_only: the app's own wrap-up words ask for 'only what the criteria still need ... or nothing', which invites a qualifier, and ADR 0112 says a 'nothing' about the criteria is nothing. Money: the person was asked for CHF 0.40 more, and the second session ran a researcher run (about CHF 0.03) that changed nothing. LC-C7's other problems are L4-money-102 (the tagline task did not run) and L4-money-104 (the Details count); merged here because LC-C7 was 'partial' for this cause first.

"Write a one-line tagline for the bakery in tagline.md" waits for your next session: "Compare ..." used the rest of this one. CHF 0.23.' More > Sessions row: '"Compare ..." paused before this session's budget of CHF 0.40 ran out.' over 'Stopped: the budget is used'. items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3544-3558: every paused result whose source stopEndsSession(...) ends the session, skips the queue and sets stopReason; packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts:241-243 counts source 'session' as ending it. A larger task capped at the work budget left gets source 'session' (executor.ts:1081), and stopSourceOf keeps it for a clean wrap-up (executor.ts:1883), although the wrap-up kept its reserve unspent. The words follow: result.ts:440-447 with oversize-words.ts:145-148 ('used the rest of this one'), stop-words.ts:138 ('Stopped: the budget is used'), result.ts:257 ('The session's budget is used.'). oversized-task.test.ts:362-369 and :391-393 assert the wrong assumption.
items.fix_sketch: In the paused branch, end the session at a 'session' source only when it cannot take more work: the run was refused at the session cap (errorCode budget_exceeded at level session), budget.noNewWork is set, or budget.workRemainingUsdMicro() is below the smallest after_large estimate. For a wrap-up pause with room left: keep the card and needs_human as today, hand the larger task's after_large items to the re-plan as takeLarger's no_room path does ('after_others'), and continue the loop so the queue-empty re-plan (cutPlanToBudget with the room left) takes those that fit. One that still does not fit reads '"B" (about CHF 0.06) waits for your next session: "Compare ..." left CHF 0.03 of this one.'. Never 'used the rest of this one', 'The session's budget is used' or 'Stopped: the budget is used' while the spent figure is under the work budget; the stop sentence follows the real reason. Update the plan wording beside runner.ts:~5335 and oversize-words.ts; change oversized-task.test.ts:362-369 and :391-393 to assert on the room left, keeping their intent (named in tests_changed_for_design). The session cap, the review reserve and the wrap-up line stay; nothing passes the work budget.
items.test_boundary: Composed real runtime (packages/runtime/test/oversized-task.test.ts, a describe 'l4-money-pause'): Big (high priority, above the work budget) then a small B under a fifth of the work budget; the stand-in wraps Big up early so it leaves more than B's estimate unspent (asserted through the ledger); expect task.started [Big, B] in one session, B done, Big needs_human with one card, stopReason not 'budget_exceeded', and none of 'used the rest of this one', "The session's budget is used", 'Stopped: the budget is used' in the result or GET /sessions/:id (today B stays ready). Real-daemon POST /sessions case in describe 'l4-money-pause, run L4' and the Sessions-row UI test: no row says both 'paused before ... ran out' and 'the budget is used'.
items.notes: Raised to major (the verdict said minor): the owner's option C of 2026-11-09 ('the session keeps its promise and spare budget isn't wasted') and the Start dialog's promise ('it runs if ... leaves budget') are broken, and three screens state money that is not true. Deterministic, not the model's: any larger task that wraps up cleanly at the session's work budget does this. The run C plan's OP-0 listed done, failed, paused at its own budget and paused without progress as the ends that hand the room on; a clean wrap-up at the session's work budget was missed.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1071-1081: sessionLeftUsdMicro = min(the token's budget, the session's work remaining), and runCapSource knows only the run's own source (task_budget, specialist_limit) or 'session'; :1129 brief.budgetUsdMicro = min(work cap, session left), never an outer limit. packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:155-170: precheck fixes the wrap-up line from claims.budgetUsdMicro (enforcement/budget.ts:247-252) before caps.check, which only refuses a call. budget-pause.ts budgetLineWords (:340) writes the start line from that figure. ADR 0112 point 6 says a stop names the limit that applies; the start line contradicts the stop it leads to.
items.fix_sketch: In LoopTaskExecutor.execute read what the outer limits still allow this run's scope (the project's budget, the month's cap; the plan share's room only through the caps port) with the level that binds, at the stop line (not the 80% room): e.g. an append-only CapsPort.remainingUsdMicro(scope) -> {usdMicro, level}. brief.budgetUsdMicro = min(work cap, session left, that remainder); runCapSource 'project' or 'month' when it binds; the token, the wrap-up line, the reserve and the stop sentence then follow one figure. When the remainder binds, keep room in it for the task's review as BA-4 does inside a task's budget (R + W when it can hold it; else the review pauses as today). budgetLineWords names the limit ('This run may spend CHF 0.06, what is left of the project's budget: ...'). The hooks' caps.check stays the backstop. Fake daemon, ADR 0112 points 4 and 7 (dated amendment), runtime.md.
items.test_boundary: Composed through the runtime the daemon uses (packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts, runOne): session budget USD 2 to 5, project budget USD 0.075 (CHF 0.06), a writer task with no budget of its own, the stand-in keeps working: the 'This run may spend' line names at most CHF 0.06, the run hears the wrap-up (heardWrapUp) and ends 'paused' with its work kept, never with a budget_exceeded Run row, and the ledger stays at or under the project's budget (today: 'This run may spend CHF 1.20 ...' and a hard stop). A twin under the month's cap. Real-daemon: the session's events through the client, beside the L3-run-10 case.
items.notes: Raised to major (the verdict said minor): the owner's D4 ('wrap up in an organized and error free way such that the work can be continued') holds today only under the task's and the session's budgets; under a project budget or the month's cap the run gets a hard stop, and the start line's money figure is wrong. No money passes today (caps.check refuses), and none may after the fix: the change only lowers a run's cap. Decided without an owner question: keeping review room inside a binding outer limit is BA-4's rule applied to the limit that binds (the owner's answer of 2026-11-16 counts the reviews in what a task costs). The share's stop and its words stay l4-cred-engine's.

items.title: A review-only pass is priced as the task's whole remaining estimate, not as its review
items.what_the_person_sees: After a task paused because its review did not fit its budget, the next session's plan line, the Start dialog and the session review price the review-only pass at the task's whole estimate less its kept work (the work's figure), not at what its review should cost; the session review then measures the review against that figure.
items.evidence: C3:C3L-1 (/tmp/frbench/leftovers-C3.json, carried from run L3's L3-left-12; note of 2026-11-16: buildable after C4b).

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:569-593 questionsOutcome: once the task is done it writes 'is done' and then the start clause stored when the card was answered; the S-2 rewrite (:578-581) turns 'it joins ...' into 'what waits on it joins ...' without checking on_answer (a specialist's card prepared the task itself), ctx.waiting or whether a session still runs, and a hands-off 'started' is not rewritten, so it lands after 'is done'; the same in the 'without' branch (:582-584) and in retryOutcome's accept branch (:493-499: '"T" is done; what comes after it a session started for it (...)'). views.ts requestContexts reads the running facts only for open cards.
items.fix_sketch: One helper (doneThenStarted(card, ctx)) for every Done or Answered line that adds start words after 'is done': a specialist's card (on_answer not 'done') once its task is done says 'Answers saved in the decision record; "X" is done.' ('"X" is done without your answers.'), or for a hands-off start the events in order ('Answers sent: a session started for "X" by itself (this project starts by itself when work is ready); it is done.'); a person's own task keeps 'what waits on it ...' only while ctx.waiting is not empty and never repeats a stored 'joins the session that is running' unless a session runs now; retryOutcome's accept branch uses the same helper. Each line at most 160 characters; the fake daemon and inbox.test.tsx's Answered lines follow.
items.test_boundary: Real-daemon (GET /inbox's answered list through the client): a specialist task nothing depends on asks during a running session, the person answers (the Done line '... goes on with them; it joins the session that is running.'), the task finishes and the session ends: the Answered outcome equals 'Answers saved in the decision record; "<task>" is done.' (today the screenshot's sentence); with project.start_by_itself on, the outcome has the events in order and does not match /is done; a session started for it/. Unit (request-words): a specialist card {answered, joined, on_answer ready} and {without, ...} with taskStatus done; a person card with and without waiting; a critic:signoff accept with start_by hands_off never prints 'what comes after it a session started'.
items.notes: Merged: both come from questionsOutcome's done branch reusing a start clause stored at answer time (L4-session-13's verdict names L4-session-6 as related). Minor for the false clause (design section 5 rule 4); the order half alone would be words.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/recovery.ts:309-323 posts the Update as a plain message (body only; MessageRow, packages/state/src/types.ts:354-368, has no action) and the Inbox's Updates row (apps/ui/src/pages/InboxPage.tsx ~:700-723) offers only Mark read; recovery.ts:181 appends session.ended at recovery time (AppendEventOptions, packages/state/src/repos/event.ts:8-12, has no createdAt) although the recovery computes last_worked_at (:165).
items.fix_sketch: (a) The crash Update's Continue: the inbox view derives MessageView.action {kind: continue_session, projectId, sessionId} (append-only api-types, client, contracts, fake daemon) from what the recovery writes (the message's project_id and a reference to the interrupted session; no migration if the row's existing columns carry it, else 0011); one Update per project when several projects had tasks released; the Updates row shows a primary Continue that opens the Start dialog for the project with continues: sessionId (the same person start as the wait block's Continue, POST /sessions with continues, ADR 0118); hidden when a session of the project runs or none of the released tasks is still ready; the Update is marked read on the press. (b) The end line's time: session.ended carries the moment the session last worked (an append-only createdAt option fed with handoff.last_worked_at), or the line says the restart ('Forerunner started again after closing during this session: nothing done. CHF 0.01.'). user-guide.md (~:910-913) and runtime.md.
items.test_boundary: Real-daemon restart case (~:7013, after 'Your last session was interrupted when Forerunner closed. "Contact page in contact.html" is ready again.'): the inbox message carries action Continue; the UI suite (InboxPage against the fake and the real daemon): the Update row shows Continue, the click opens the Start dialog, confirming posts /sessions with continues=<the interrupted session's id>, and the started session runs the released task (today only Mark read). Composed restart on the simulated clock (packages/runtime/test/session-recovery.test.ts): last step at T, the clock moves 2 minutes (and 3 days): the page's last line carries T or says Forerunner started again; never 'Interrupted: Forerunner closed' at T+2 min.
items.notes: Design section 5's crash 'after' example ends '[Continue]'; run C's plan (d1109-starts-engine's decisions) counted 'the recovery Update's Continue' as a person start, never built. Continue is the person's start (D6): it starts only on the press.

items.fix_sketch: One place per fact (design section 5 rule 10), the bar being on every page (D8): while a session waits, the bar's row and Working now keep the wait with Cancel and its visible explanation, and the project's status line keeps the fact without its own Cancel ('Waiting until 15:40, then it goes on'); while it runs, the status line uses the bar's words (runText) with the progress count ('the coder works on "Create index.html" (0 of 7 done)'); the session page's Current task reads the run indicator's state ('The critic checks "X"', 'Picks the next task'); the Overview's Last result shows 'Running now: Open the session' while the first session runs. The fake daemon follows.
items.test_boundary: UI tests against the fake daemon plus a real-daemon case for the status line's text: an Overview with a waiting session has exactly one Cancel for the wait outside the bar (Playwright at 375 and 1280 px, no horizontal scroll); the status line's text equals the bar's runText plus the count; SessionPage while the critic reviews shows the bar's state, not 'Choosing the next task…'; SummaryTab during the first session shows no 'No session yet.'.
items.notes: C5L-11 was left by session lead decision 50 until LC-C31 had looked; LC-C31 saw the wait three times with three Cancels at both widths. The default above (the status line keeps the fact and drops its Cancel while the bar shows it) is the one C5L-11 suggested; the session lead confirms it before the fix starts (decision 50 is the session lead's call). Merged because all three have one cause: screens beside the bar word the running state themselves instead of reading the run indicator. run-indicator.ts and run-wait-words.ts are not changed here (l4-cred-engine and l4-cred-screens own their wait words); this item only reads them.

(5) The reviewer is the only registry specialist with no write tool (evals/registry/specialists/reviewer/specialist.md allowed_tools: cc:Read, cc:Bash, cc:Grep, cc:Glob), and ADR 0109's rule exists only as prompt text: reviewer/specialist.md:29-31 ('You write no file, not even a review file a brief names'), evals/registry/principals/project-manager.md:52 (the planner) and docs/decisions/0109-a-reviewers-findings-are-its-report.md. So the app tells the reviewer two opposite things and the critic grades against the app's text: not the model's choice.
items.fix_sketch: (a) One helper from the registry, not a name: writesNoFile(profile) is true when no allowed tool maps to write_file (packages/runtime/src/registry/tools.ts' mapping; today only the reviewer). (b) outcomeCriterion gains the specialist's writesNoFile: for such a specialist it says the report stands for any file the outcome names (proposed: 'The report shows this outcome (this specialist writes no file, so a file named here is met by its report): <outcome>'), the same text in the brief and in the critic's evidence; every other specialist keeps today's text byte for byte. (c) GET /settings/models adds an append-only field per specialist (for example writesNoFile: string | null) with the daemon's words: 'The reviewer writes no file: its findings are its report, which you read in the task's drawer.' New task shows it as its own line under Who does it when that specialist is chosen (beside, never instead of, the runs-on or limitation line); Edit asks with the project and the edited words and shows the same line under edit-who. Creating or saving the task is never refused. (d) Cut line: when the typed outcome or criteria name a file to write ('review.md lists ...', 'write/create ... review.md'), the line names it ('..., so review.md is not written: ...'); an input file ('found in notes/plan.md') never triggers it (golden set of phrasings). (e) Cut line, sibling: chat's task.create / task.edit read-back for a reviewer adds the same clause. ADR 0109 gets a dated amendment: decision 1 covers the tasks the person makes (New task, Edit, chat) and the criterion of a task with no criteria.

items.notes: Not model_only: the app's own criterion asked the reviewer for a file its prompt forbids, and the critic graded against the app's criterion. Severity minor (the verdict's): cheap (CHF 0.04 here), the reviewer's report said so honestly, the person was asked. Caveat from the verdict: in this run the 'could not do' and the grade of 10 come mostly from notes/plan.md missing, which the repro planted on purpose; the write rule is the second reason, but with the plan present the task still could not meet its criterion. items.title: Forerunner's snapshot refs (refs/forerunner/before|first/<task id>) in a folder project's git
items.what_the_person_sees: Nothing with plain git: `git log` in the project's folder shows 'Workspace before "<title>"' with no id (live check 4, LC-L3.L3-run-11 PASS: 'no UUID, no ISO instant (0 matches)'). Only git older than 2.39, `git log --clear-decorations`, `log.initialDecorationSet=all` or a GUI that draws every ref (gitk --all) shows labels like 'refs/forerunner/before/01a1...' on those commits.
items.evidence: /tmp/frbench/leftovers-L3.json LL-11; /tmp/frbench/runL3-l3-small-review.json (non_blocking: 'same class as the existing wip and set-aside refs; git 2.43 here hides them') and runL3-l3-small-fixup.json; at 4cf11fd packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:716-731 (snapshotRef, firstSnapshotRef) set at :2651-2655, read at packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts:309 and packages/runtime/src/loop/project-checks.ts:206. Checked here with git 2.43 on a scratch repository under /tmp/frbench: `git log --oneline --decorate` and `git log --all --oneline --decorate=full` print only 'HEAD -> main'; only `--clear-decorations` or `-c log.initialDecorationSet=all` print the refs/forerunner label.
items.root_cause_at_head: By design of run L3's L3-run-11 fix: the snapshot is found by a ref of Forerunner's own instead of an id in the commit message.
items.notes: Why not a problem: a ref name is an internal lookup key, not a sentence the system writes for the person (design section 5 lists what it covers); the commits a person reads carry no id; current git (2.39 and later, as current Git for Windows ships) does not decorate refs outside heads, remotes, tags and stash by default; the same family (wip, set-aside, failed, deps, rebuilt) has existed since earlier waves and no live check found a person meeting it; and the snapshot commits are on the folder's own branch, so the refs add no commits to `git log --all`. A key built from the title would collide between same-titled tasks and move with an Edit. If a later round tidies refs, before/ and first/ can be deleted once a task is done or cancelled (they serve its runs' review and project checks), keeping first/ while a Redo is possible.

decisions: One verdict per Agent SDK stream, whether it ends normally or throws: a refusal is provider_auth (refused, one card, the task waits), a usage limit is the subscription's rest, and an error_max_budget_usd is a budget stop. A bare 401 in a run's own output still does not count. Claude Code's synthetic error message is not a model call.

The subscription's share reached mid-run is a credential stop like a usage limit: reason share, until the month's start (UTC), named in the person's zone or the end of quiet hours. Under next the work goes on on the key from its kept work; under ask, one card; under wait, the person's session goes on by itself at the month's start (decisions 8, 21 and 22). The plan-level budget card is no longer used for the share.

A notification about a card says what the card's own view says, built from the same context as the Inbox, in the person's zone read at that moment. A card with nothing to answer points at its one action. A session whose only news is a credential wait that an open card already tells sends nothing of its own (design §4.3, §5.10).

Chat names the credential that answered only under an answer that was really given, once per stop per conversation. A failure is one sentence per error code that says what to do. Chat's hold reply says what still works and what to do, and chat's start follows the Start dialog: refused where it refuses, kept for the reset where it keeps.

The person's time zone and the monthly cap are read at each use, never captured when the daemon starts. Time comes from the Clock (RouteContext.nowMs required; no Date.now() fallback in credential code).
A call is booked on the credential that served it, finished or cut off.
The configured Anthropic API address covers every call, subscription task runs included (only when it is not the default).
A waiting session queued behind another project's session is the next one on the running bar, and its own line says it goes on after that session.

CE-6 is built here, as session lead decision 48 sent it to this triage: the share reached mid-run is a run-out under the person's policy (the owner's D5: 'Running out includes a usage limit, a plan-share cap and a monthly cap'); until it is built nothing passes the share, because the share is held at every pick.

decisions: Money first (owner's answer of 2026-11-16: a task's budget counts its work, the critic's reviews and the fixes): a review capped by a task's budget is sized to the room left (max_tokens down to a 2,048-token minimum) instead of refused at the 8,192-token floor; nothing ever passes the task's budget, the session's budget, its wrap-up line, the monthly cap or the plan share. The session lead confirms this change to C4b's per-call floor (L4-selftasks-101).

The plan writes a model-proposed task budget that cannot hold the task's estimate including its review as that estimate, before the plan card shows it (the person sees and approves the figure; never above the session or project budget), and the plan card warns for a task still at risk (owner's answer 8: 'it should get a warning, but it should get done anyway').

The task check's evidence is exactly ADR 0119 point 3's: a report's 'For the task list:' lines, a critic finding the task did not cause (NOT_CAUSED_BY_TASK, or an explicit critic flag) and kept notes; an ordinary critic note about the task's own work is not evidence. The check after the session's last task stays (ADR 0119 point 8).

A line that reads like an instruction is quoted to the person even when the check changes nothing (ADR 0119 point 4): on the task check's own session log line, which becomes person level with its cost (ADR 0119 point 9; this answers C4L-15), and in chat's reply; no new Inbox card (session lead default; an information-only card stays the lead's option).
The model's flagged entries are its own words: shown as what the agent's check noted, never as 'a line of the report'.

The check's message carries each named task's outcome and, inside the data envelope, the person's brief; the critic's review request carries what the person gave (their brief and answers, with the decision record path) as data. Run C's 'titles, criteria, status words and report lines only' rule is widened on purpose (ADR 0119 point 5 dated note).

Kept as built (session lead decisions): the task check stays out of every task's budget (runC-plan session_lead_decisions[32]); flagged-only evidence makes no call (decision 33); a task the person wrote gets a suggestion card at every level (decision 34); the drawer-only reason line (decision 54).

L4-money-303 (C4bD-1) is built inside L4-selftasks-101 (one root: runner.ts:4863's room check before the review counts only the output cap): the room check before the critic's checks counts the first call's input too, so below the minimum whole price no check runs and the card is the same review-waits card.

questionsReason is changed once for both live reports (L4-money-302 and L4-selftasks-112 (a); one function, person-questions.ts:382-401): quoted spans do not count toward the match, REASON_WORDS gains 'does not exist', 'not allowed', 'could not' and their kin, open sections and sentences that say the person must supply something win ties, and no REASON_WORDS bonus inside a Summary.

L4-selftasks-105's chat reply half (a Yes whose composed set is refused says which changes were not made and why) is l4-selftasks-chat's (L4f): it lives in agent.ts' confirm branch or the commands executor's composed-perform sentence, both that area's this round; this area makes sure no no-op edit ever enters a set (the fence compares fields; callsOf skips an empty edit; proposalLine names only changed fields).
Moved out (session lead): L4-selftasks-107 (one estimate per plan) to l4-money-pause, beside L4-money-104 (same root: the session's size is its promise).

The critic prompt's change of meaning (L4-selftasks-106, and L4-selftasks-102's flag if built) bumps critic.md to 1.4.0 and is re-calibrated live in phase F (F-16), as docs/maintainers/critic.md:548-550 says; the fake-provider calibration stays green here (D-L4-27).

Security: never weaken the hooks or the sandbox; text from pages, searches, files, cards, chat history, reports, pull request bodies or any record never becomes instructions to a model: it enters a request only inside the data envelope, scanned and redacted as today, and a flagged line never reaches a model; no credential value, token, fingerprint or source id appears in a sentence, a log or a test snapshot (pnpm secrets:scan). Text from reports, critic notes, the model's flagged entries, the person's brief and answers, cards, chat history and records enters a request only inside the data envelope, redacted as briefs are; the strict schema and the fence hold whatever the model returns; the check's call has no tools; report-007 in pnpm test:injection fails on today's code and passes after. Money: no budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or plan-share cap is ever passed or raised by this area; every model call it adds or moves is booked in CHF on the credential that served it, inside the room the session's promise leaves; a wait moves nothing. A review sized to the room never exceeds the task's budget (minimum 2,048 output tokens, never above 8,192; the hooks' precheck stays the backstop); a raised plan budget is shown on the plan card before approval and never above the session's or the project's budget; every task check stays a booked Run row in CHF inside the room after the session's promise; the change to C4b's per-call floor is the session lead's (this plan's decisions). decisions: A yes is judged against what the person was shown: the stored 'at most' is the CHF on the line (rounded up to the centime); a Go ahead re-asks only when the model changed or the shown figure would change; the pass's budget is the yes's 'at most', capped by the room.

The fast model never asks in words: the thinking_longer fact and answer_thoroughly's definition say who acts. An ask-only backstop in code (a dated amendment to ADR 0114's 'Who decides', for the session lead's review): a typed quick answer that ended without answer_thoroughly on a line whose words show a failure, plan, comparison or review need gets the app's own ask line with Go ahead when the rung asks first, or Think it through when it would go ahead; a pattern never spends, nothing runs before the person's yes (the owner's answer 2: 'warn/ask first').

The thorough pass is told what it is: its own facts line ('this_answer: the closer look on Sonnet the person said yes to ...') in place of the quick pass's thinking_longer line, and CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES saying it is the closer look; the fast request stays byte-identical.
Answer now never earns a next-rung offer; only a pass whose budget line wrapped it up does.
The history window moves in steps of 6 turns, a pure function of the stored rows (the same after a restart), so quick turns read the history from the prompt cache.
A project closed by Make one project takes no new work from any route: the plan route, the Data tab's add and import, and a Yes answered after the join (the joined sentence).
task.dependencies says when the task runs; removing its last undone dependency prepares work (joins a running session if it fits, ADR 0118 point 3).
Money in chat's start read-back and its done sentence has two decimals (§5 rule 7); design §5's 'Chat read-back' After example becomes '(up to CHF 5.00)' (the session lead's design_doc_changes).
chat_ask_above keeps its value and its meaning apart in every sentence; an offer line that is no longer the newest reads in the past with no question.

The ask-only backstop (L4-chat-202) is approved as a dated amendment to ADR 0114's 'Who decides' (this plan's decisions): it only attaches the app's own ask line; nothing spends before the person's yes (the owner's answer 2 of 2026-11-09: 'if it will switch models and do an expensive task, it should warn/ask first').

Security: never weaken the hooks or the sandbox; text from pages, searches, files, cards, chat history, reports, pull request bodies or any record never becomes instructions to a model: it enters a request only inside the data envelope, scanned and redacted as today, and a flagged line never reaches a model; no credential value, token, fingerprint or source id appears in a sentence, a log or a test snapshot (pnpm secrets:scan). The backstop only attaches an offer the gate allows; a record's words never start a spend (the gate's injection and recordsRead checks stay first); a closed project's guard holds on every path, a Yes answered after the join included. Money: no budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or plan-share cap is ever passed or raised by this area; every model call it adds or moves is booked in CHF on the credential that served it, inside the room the session's promise leaves; a wait moves nothing. A yes covers at most the CHF on its line; nothing is spent before the person's yes on a stronger rung or above their amount; the stepped history window never sends more than the history token budget. decisions: A bare 'yes' keeps design §3.9's state: with no card and no app offer waiting it is never handed to the model and gets 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes. Say what you want done, for example "run it now" to start a session.' (0 model calls). Chat's own asks are removed at their cause instead: a change asked for in words is an 'asks' claim the guard nudges into its command (read back with Yes and No), a lookup offer is L4-chat-101's absence guard (look it up, never ask), a hand-over offer is L4-chat-202's app ask with Go ahead, and the prompt says never to ask for a yes in words. Design §3.9 and agent.ts:1215-1219 stay as they are (the plan check, D-L4-23: the triage's forwarded yes reversed the design without a recorded decision).

The claim guard gains two kinds: 'asks' (a yes asked for in words to make a change) and 'absent' (a 'not there / can't find / Should I look?' reply in a turn that offered recall and called neither recall tool); one nudge each, inside the turn's model calls and its budget; a claim still standing gives the true line as today. Clarifying questions stay free.

Prompt (conversation-agent.md, this area's sections, and CHAT_RECALL_RULES): look it up in this turn instead of offering to; never ask for a yes in words; only the app writes 'The app did:'; never describe tool calls, their order or refusals; never name a tool; all asserted verbatim on the request.

Recall's lines are worded as the screens word them: a session line names its failed tasks; a questions card's line carries its question; the From line names the records the reply rests on among the turn's hits, opened or strong and named by title (ADR 0114 'Sources', dated amendment).

After Cancel the stored session result is read through run-indicator's resultAfterWait wherever chat (facts, 'summary', Read aloud from chat) and the Overview read it; one rule, reached from commands through a port.

'open <project>' in a project's Chat tab opens that project's page, as the New project dialog's Open it does (D1: lead the person to the project that already uses the repository); 'switch to <project>' keeps U-056 and says 'This chat stays about <tab's project>.' with an Open link; a pronoun never matches a project by substring.
A joined project's lessons reach the kept project's sessions through the same withJoined scope chat uses; nothing is moved or copied (ADR 0117's amendment kept).
Kept until the owner answers: the app's own chat lines stay English (L4-chat-310); a project whose card chat sees in full keeps reading back every change (L4-chat-309).

'add a task: ...' keeps acting at once with Undo (U-015); naming a project ('to Site:') adds there; a pronoun target ('there', 'it', 'dort') resolves to the project switched to in this conversation, or chat asks 'Which project: Notes or Site?' with the projects as options (L4-selftasks-119, moved here from l4-selftasks-chat so that one area owns how chat names a target project: matchAddTask, matchSwitch and matchProjects' pronoun rule).

The chat model never writes a read-back or 'The app did:' itself (L4-selftasks-118, merged into L4-chat-102 and L4-chat-112): the history shows the app's acts as the app's lines ('The app asked, with Yes and No: ...'); the claim guard catches an imitated read-back question as an 'asks' claim and a forged change line as a false claim, nudges once, and otherwise replies that nothing changed; a forged marker is stripped and never reaches the next turn's history.

A bare yes never reaches the model (design §3.9; the forwarded yes was dropped in the plan check, D-L4-23); recall's results stay inside the untrusted envelope and the injection scan (a card's question can carry planted words: L4-chat-107's injection case); a forged 'The app did:' line can no longer pose as a change in history; pnpm test:injection stays green with no case or judge weakened. Money: no budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or plan-share cap is ever passed or raised by this area; every model call it adds or moves is booked in CHF on the credential that served it, inside the room the session's promise leaves; a wait moves nothing. Every nudge is a model call inside CHAT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS and the turn's budget. Docs in the same commits: docs/maintainers/runtime.md (chat: the guard's kinds, the asks claim, the bare yes kept, recall lines, sources, history leads), commands.md (the summary port, project switch, matchProjects, matchAddTask's target), apps.md (Conversation's switch navigation; :582's header line corrected), memory.md (the project-id set), docs/user-guide.md (Chat, Overview), ADR 0114 dated amendments (the yes rule, the claim guard's new kinds, Sources), ADR 0117 (lessons of a joined project). Never edit CHANGELOG.md, docs/status/UPDATE-LOG.md, docs/requirements.md or docs/design/core-experience.md: they are the session lead's (run C decision 19); put suggested lines, U-entry Check in the app steps and design_doc_changes in the report. No real model and no real GitHub writes in this area: phase F checks the parts only the real model or real GitHub show. decisions: One figure for 'the waiting work', from one function in start-check.ts: the runnable tasks, the larger task's room and the later followers, plus the claimed tasks priced with their review part (the owner's answer of 2026-11-16) less all they spent, capped at the work budget. The ask card, the Start dialog's Use API key line and the plan card's foot line all show it. The dialog keeps the plan sentence beside the stop line.

The yes on 'Use your API key until ...?' lets in only the tasks that waited for that stop. Other ready work joins the running session only if it fits (option C). Work the agent adds during the session stays bounded by its budget (D7), and the card keeps 'for what waits now' (the owner's answer 3: the yes is for all work until the stop ends).
A wait for the one credential that can do a task says why ('Waits for your API key: only it can read web pages here.'). The wait record carries the need, and it is read the same after a restart.

Under 'next' the Start dialog names the stop in either direction ('Your API key is at its limit until 11:57, so this runs on your subscription (about CHF 0.07).'). '(costs money)' follows only the API key.
'Start on 1 Dec' keeps the start for the share and key-month stops as 'Start at 15:40' does for a limit. 'Change the allowance' is wherever the share wait shows.
The one-off press answers the held question in place: one person line, and the model sees the question once.
The UI's clocks use the person's zone from GET /me, the same zone as the daemon's sentences.

Credential words: CHF under a centime reads 'less than CHF 0.01' on every line. Consequence lines are at most 100 characters. A line names the button that is on the screen. A kept start is not called a continuation.

decisions: A removed project uses nothing (ADR 0117 point 2): its take-over and joined ids no longer make an id known, so New project on its repository gets the offer again; a joined project's take-over still counts through its keeper; run C session lead decision 14 (a removed project frees its repository; the marker that names the removed project itself is replaced by the next project's first docs pull request) is kept. Why: the owner's D1 and D9.

The scaffold branch starts from the default branch whenever no scaffold pull request of this project is open, as the status branch does. Forerunner never force-pushes over a branch it did not write for this project (D-L4-24): when fr/docs-scaffold on GitHub is not this project's own (another project's marker, or none), the docs pull request opens on fr/docs-scaffold-<project slug> from the default branch without force and the old branch and its closed pull request stay as they are; a force-push (with a lease, never the default branch) replaces only this project's own scaffold or intake branch. Another project's open pull request is never touched (W15-01). A take-over while this project's own scaffold pull request is open rebuilds that branch on the default branch before the replaced marker is written (ADR 0117's amendment). Why: GitHub keeps closed pull requests' head branches by default, and a closed pull request's branch can be another project's or another person's.

A take-over whose docs pull request did not open says so where the person reads the take-over (repo.take_over's sentence, the Overview's line, Docs), never "Took over ..." alone. Why: design section 5 rule 9.

A together project cannot turn on the status pull request: settings.set refuses in one sentence at the command (Settings, chat and voice alike) and Settings shows no switch for it. Why: D9 (a together project writes nothing to the repository).

The first-plan form needs the decision record; the cut-off advice keeps it short instead of dropping it; the plan-only form (Add to) writes no docs. Why: the plan card shows the decision before approval (design section 3.3).

Add to answers at once and plans in the background, as a new project's plan does (L4-github-106); the Overview's one place for the pending plan (the banner with Open) is l4-money-pause's L4-github-110, built in L4c: this area's drafting state uses that banner as it finds it.
No possessive after a quoted name; a consequence line at most 100 characters; the configured host, never a hardcoded one. Why: design section 5 rules 1 and 6, run L3's L3-github-8, AGENTS.md.

Security: never weaken the hooks or the sandbox; text from pages, searches, files, cards, chat history, reports, pull request bodies or any record never becomes instructions to a model: it enters a request only inside the data envelope, scanned and redacted as today, and a flagged line never reaches a model; no credential value, token, fingerprint or source id appears in a sentence, a log or a test snapshot (pnpm secrets:scan). decisions: A dependency whose reviewed change reached main through a pull request merged on GitHub is recorded as merged through it (state merged, last_outcome merged_through, no migration), in whatever order the watcher reads the two events and across a restart; one card says it with Take this work out and Keep it; nothing is written to GitHub before the person presses. Why: design section 5 rule 4; ADR 0111 point 4 left it for later.

Every merge card of a task closes when its pull request is closed on GitHub, as on a merge (ADR 0111 2026-11-15 point 3), Answered "Closed: #33 was closed on GitHub.". Why: U-028 (every option does what it says). The same close of a cancelled task's pull request is recorded as a merge record with last_outcome closed, so chat's facts read 'Closed without merging' (L4-chat-110, merged into L4-github-117: same root, nothing records a close made on GitHub).

The press reads each pull request of the chain once before it answers: its checks and mergeable state (L4-github-118) and its branch head through host.getBranchHead, never only the listing's lagging head (L4-creds-22, merged into L4-github-118: the same press block); a failed check, a conflict or a head newer than the reviewed commit is refused at once in the merge step's own words; nothing merges a pull request whose check failed; the merge PUT stays pinned to the sha.

After a join the kept project lists the closing project's open status pull request (Open, Merge) whatever its own setting; the status writer still writes there only once the setting is on; the dialog names the status setting. Why: ADR 0117 point 3 ("one status pull request again") and the dialog's own promise that the pull requests move.
The dialog's open pull request count reads one predicate with the task row: a record closed on GitHub is not open.

Costs' runs and accepted runs of a task are the task's own, wherever its ledger rows are booked; money, totals and the other groupings stay the project's own ledger (BA-9, OJ-07). Accepted counts tries (L4-money-301, moved here: the same task-run helper): a run that paused and that a later run of the same task continued is one try with it, for By task, the specialist and the model alike; no money figure changes.
A joined or removed project's page names itself in the header, never shows an internal folder, and its Last result says where its tasks went. Why: design sections 3.1 and 5 rules 3 and 4.
A merge the press found already made on GitHub reads "#59 was merged on GitHub already."; only Forerunner's own reads "Merged #59.". Why: ADR 0111 point 3.
The held hands-off join refusal is one sentence of at most 100 characters (L4-creds-28, moved here beside L4-github-113's join-words lines).

OWNER 2026-11-18 (L4-github-130): Close beside Open on the 'Cancelled, still open on GitHub' row, with its one-line consequence ('Closes this pull request on GitHub; you can reopen it there.'); it closes only that pull request, on GitHub with the project's own token, never deletes its branch, and the row goes once GitHub answers; amend ADR 0105 point 4 (dated).

Security: never weaken the hooks or the sandbox; text from pages, searches, files, cards, chat history, reports, pull request bodies or any record never becomes instructions to a model: it enters a request only inside the data envelope, scanned and redacted as today, and a flagged line never reaches a model; no credential value, token, fingerprint or source id appears in a sentence, a log or a test snapshot (pnpm secrets:scan). Never weaken the push guard; marker names stay cleaned data; the token never appears in a log, an error or a sentence; another project's open pull request is never written to or commented on (W15-01); a together project writes nothing to the repository (D9); nothing is written to GitHub except what the person presses (Merge, Take this work out); the press's added reads are read-only; a pull request whose check failed is never merged. Money: no budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or plan-share cap is ever passed or raised by this area; every model call it adds or moves is booked in CHF on the credential that served it, inside the room the session's promise leaves; a wait moves nothing. Default kept: a change that acts at once on the person's words is theirs too. The proposal still runs as the agent, so the limit-always-asks rule (ADR 0030 item 2) is unchanged.

Read-back lifetime (D-L4-12 as revised in the plan check; run C decision 53; design §3.9): every chat read-back lives until it is answered or another read-back replaces it, across a restart; its Yes is decided again on the current state and applies only what it read back while that is unchanged (a fix set: the task-list fingerprint, 'The tasks changed since I checked them; say "fix the tasks" to check again.'; any other: the named tasks' or settings' fields, else one line saying what changed and asking again). Any expiry that remains is shown (events, one Update, the open chat drops Yes). ADR 0030 point 3 gets a dated amendment.
A change waiting for a yes is said once, by the card (design section 3.9); the model's prose about it is dropped.
A note is the person's only when the person wrote it; the chat model is told to pass only the person's words and any note it passes is read back.
Kept as built: the drawer-only reason line (decision 54, C6L-17); 'Fix the tasks' is chat only (owner question 8 of run C still open).

A Continue or a wake starts only what the person's press or setting allows (D6); the questions card's quote stays quoted data; chat's list of the card's options is the app's own words. Money: no budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or plan-share cap is ever passed or raised by this area; every model call it adds or moves is booked in CHF on the credential that served it, inside the room the session's promise leaves; a wait moves nothing. The crash Continue goes on with what is left of the interrupted session's budget or starts a fresh one the person confirms in the Start dialog, never more; a too-large task never reads that it may join. Docs in the same commits: docs/maintainers/runtime.md, state.md (the listed rule), commands.md, apps.md; docs/decisions/0116 (point 5 and rule 10, dated amendments) and 0118 (too_large, the limit wake, the crash Continue); docs/user-guide.md (the Inbox card paragraph, the crash paragraph, the sessions list paragraph). owner_questions_carried.question: Owner (D3, after your answer 2): chat now thinks longer as needed, with no daily amount of its own; its spend counts against the project's budget as well as the monthly cap, as all chat spend does today. Should longer answers count only against the monthly cap, so thinking in chat never takes budget from the project's work?
owner_questions_carried.default_kept: Counted against the project's budget and the monthly cap; chat asks first before a stronger model or an answer over CHF 0.10.
